base_properties.human_readable: Autonomy-Rights Dignity Settlement in AI Safeguarding

stakeholders.name: data_protection_regulators
stakeholders.situation: Draft and enforce the rules requiring AI systems to disclose automated decisions, obtain consent for data processing, and pass conformity assessments. Their budgets and careers depend on administering the regime; they can adjust rules and penalties but operate inside treaties and statutes they did not write and cannot unilaterally abandon.

stakeholders.name: individual_data_subjects
stakeholders.situation: Receive enforceable claims against AI-driven decisions about credit, employment, and essential services, plus rights to access and delete their data. They pay in attention and time: consent prompts, privacy policies, and complaint procedures place the burden of policing compliance on each person individually. Opting out of datafied services entirely is impractical, so participation is effectively compulsory.

stakeholders.name: digital_rights_organizations
stakeholders.situation: Litigate, lobby, and publish scorecards in the framework's rights vocabulary; their funding, membership, and public standing flow from the regime's existence. Their organizational mission is constituted by advancing rights-based protection, so reorienting to a different normative register would dissolve the organization's purpose rather than relocate it.

stakeholders.name: incumbent_ai_platforms
stakeholders.situation: Absorb compliance costs that scale far less than proportionally with firm size, converting fixed regulatory obligations into a relative advantage over smaller rivals for whom the same obligations are existential. They shape standards through consultation processes and revolving-door expertise, shift processing and launches across jurisdictions toward favorable regimes, and sell the compliance tooling their competitors must also buy.

stakeholders.name: small_ai_developers
stakeholders.situation: Face the same documentation, assessment, and consent-infrastructure obligations as incumbents without legal teams or compliance departments. For many, multi-jurisdiction conformity costs exceed product-development budgets; the practical options are narrowing scope to a single friendly jurisdiction, selling to a larger firm, or exiting.

stakeholders.name: algorithmically_managed_workers
stakeholders.situation: Work under scheduling, evaluation, and task-allocation algorithms. The framework grants them individual complaint routes and disclosure rights but no collective voice over the systems themselves; pursuing a claim means months of procedure against an employer who controls the evidence. Leaving platform-mediated labor markets entirely is rarely feasible.

stakeholders.name: compliance_industry
stakeholders.situation: Auditors, consultancies, and legal practices whose revenue comes from the certifications, impact assessments, and remediation work the rules require. Demand tracks the strictness of the regime; they serve clients across jurisdictions and would redeploy to adjacent assurance markets if demand shifted.

stakeholders.name: faith_based_bioethics_advocates
stakeholders.situation: Hold that personhood protections derive from sources the regulatory process does not recognize as admissible inputs. Consultation channels accept submissions only in the framework's own terms, so their contributions arrive already translated or are set aside. Their objection is constitutive of their tradition, so abandoning the vocabulary is not available to them.

stakeholders.name: posthumanist_researchers
stakeholders.situation: Pursue enhancement, longevity, and artificial-minds research under precautionary hedges justified in terms they regard as parochial. Funding, ethics-board approval, and publication run through institutions governed by the framework; arguing for wider permissions requires conceding its premises, and their careers advance inside those institutions.

stakeholders.name: technology_ethics_scholars
stakeholders.situation: Map how the framework performs across jurisdictions, publish critiques of consent formalism and compliance asymmetry, and supply the comparative evidence that regulators and litigants cite. They hold no stake in the regime's revenue or penalties.

six_questions.coordination_function: Solves the collective-action problem of AI development racing to the bottom on manipulation, surveillance, and labor exploitation by giving regulators, developers, and deployers a shared, portable standard — transparency, consent, data-subject rights, disclosure of automated decision-making — for when automated treatment of persons is permissible.
six_questions.transfer_function: Moves compliance costs and adjudication burdens from AI developers toward regulators and individuals; moves decision authority over acceptable AI conduct from deployers to rights-holders and their representatives; moves legitimacy and hearing time toward claims framed in rights vocabulary and away from claims framed in other registers.
six_questions.absent_voices: Faith-based bioethics bodies and posthumanist researchers sit outside the consultative loop: their dignity claims must be recast into rights vocabulary before they are admissible, and many are never submitted at all. Workers in jurisdictions without enforcement capacity are formally covered but practically voiceless. They are in seminaries and theology faculties, transhumanist and AI-lab research networks, and informal labor markets.
six_questions.disappearance_rationale: If the autonomy-rights safeguarding regime vanished overnight, AI deployment would reorganize around whatever filled the vacuum — platform self-regulation, jurisdictional competition, and private arbitration. Data practices, workplace algorithmic management, enhancement oversight, and the litigation and advocacy economies built on the rights register would all rearrange within a few years.
six_questions.founding_problem: Twentieth-century atrocities showed that protecting persons by appeal to status, capability, or divine order fails precisely when states and markets deny those grounds; the postwar settlement grounded protection in the autonomous rights-bearing person instead. As AI systems began making consequential decisions about people — credit, employment, criminal justice — that ground was extended to demand transparency, consent, and contestability from automated decision-making.
six_questions.founding_problem_corroboration: Corroborated from outside the benefiting parties: court judgments applying dignity doctrine against state and corporate interests, discrimination audits of deployed algorithmic systems, and worker-surveillance studies all attest the problem is live. The sibling readings also attest liveness while disputing the ground — faith-based bodies affirm persons require protection from instrumentalization; posthumanist scholars affirm emerging kinds of persons require it.

commentary.narrative_context: The postwar dignity settlement — dignity grounded in the autonomous, rational, rights-bearing person rather than in divine image or social station — was extended, from the first data-protection laws through comprehensive privacy regimes to contemporary AI legislation, into a safeguarding apparatus for automated decision-making: transparency duties, consent requirements, data-subject rights, disclosure of algorithmic management, and cautiously permitted human enhancement within rights constraints. This story authors ONE reading of the contested dignity kernel: the autonomy-rights reading assessing the standing arrangement by its own lights. The claim and the metrics are independent authored facts: the reading CLAIMS the arrangement as a legitimate protective settlement, while the authored metrics describe its actual mixed operation — real protection coexisting with consent formalism, compliance asymmetry, and procedural closure against rival dignity vocabularies. The engine computes per-seat classifications from the structural data; the divergence between the claim and the metrics is the datum, not an error.
key_agents: - data_protection_regulators: Agenda-setter (institutional/constrained) — drafts and enforces the transparency, consent, and assessment rules; cannot exit the framework they administer
- incumbent_ai_platforms: Primary beneficiary with payer overlay (institutional/arbitrage) — converts fixed compliance costs into scale advantage and shapes the standards
- individual_data_subjects: Protected class paying the consent burden (powerless/constrained) — receives enforceable claims, pays in attention and procedure
- algorithmically_managed_workers: Heaviest target among the protected (powerless/trapped) — individual complaint routes against employers who control the evidence
- small_ai_developers: Payer (moderate/constrained) — bears disproportionate conformity costs relative to size
- digital_rights_organizations: Beneficiary (organized/identity_locked) — mission constituted by the rights register itself
- compliance_industry: Beneficiary (organized/mobile) — sells the certifications and assessments the rules require
- faith_based_bioethics_advocates: Excluded voice (organized/identity_locked) — divine-image ground inadmissible in the consultative process
- posthumanist_researchers: Excluded voice (moderate/constrained) — enhancement and synthetic-minds programs hedged by premises they do not share
- technology_ethics_scholars: Analytical observer — supplies the comparative evidence all seats cite
commentary.logic_rationale: Extractiveness is moderate (0.46 at interval end) because the arrangement delivers real, valued protection while simultaneously shifting enforcement burden onto individuals and converting fixed compliance costs into incumbent advantage; from this reading's own lights the arrangement is largely legitimate, so epsilon stays well below snare-range despite the measurable asymmetries. Suppression (0.56) reflects two distinct forces: the enforcement machinery (penalties, conformity assessments) and the procedural closure that renders non-rights dignity vocabularies inadmissible — suppression is authored as a raw structural property and is deliberately NOT scaled by power or scope; only extractiveness is scaled downstream. Theater (0.42) captures consent formalism: cookie banners, boilerplate impact assessments, and ethics review that frequently ratifies rather than examines, alongside genuinely functional enforcement. Accessibility_collapse is low-moderate (0.35) because alternatives persist — sectoral regimes, jurisdictional variation, and non-rights vocabularies surviving in academic and religious discourse. Resistance (0.52) reflects sustained industry lobbying, jurisdictional competition, and dissent from the sibling readings. The measurement series run on one shared seven-point grid (all three metrics at every point); trajectories are a monotonic ratchet rather than a cycle — the comprehensive-legislation wave around t=20 visibly steepens all three series, and no intermittent-reinforcement dynamic is claimed.
commentary.perspectival_gap: The seats compute differently from the same structure. From the agenda-setter seat the arrangement is protective administration — regulators experience themselves as the remedy, not the burden. From the payer seats it operates as compulsion: small developers experience existential conformity costs, workers experience individualized complaint routes against evidence-controlling employers. From the excluded seats it operates as silencing — the framework does not defeat their claims, it makes them inadmissible before submission. From the beneficiary seats it is protection (data subjects) or revenue and moat (compliance industry, incumbents). The engine derives these divergent classifications from power, exit, and directional position; nothing in the authored claim adjudicates between them.
commentary.directionality_logic: Beneficiary declarations drive low directionality for data subjects, rights organizations, and the compliance industry; victim declarations drive high directionality for small developers, algorithmically managed workers, and the two excluded groups, whose exclusion is the enforcement object of the framework's admissibility rules. Two dual-positioned agents are carried by secondary_role rather than directionality overrides, because the override surface keys on power atoms and both seats share atoms with cleanly-derived counterparts: incumbent_ai_platforms (institutional, like the regulators) is a net beneficiary whose payer overlay is recorded in role and situation; individual_data_subjects (powerless, like the workers) is a net beneficiary whose consent burden is likewise recorded. Scope amplification applies modestly at the global scope most seats occupy; the engine owns that arithmetic.
commentary.mandatrophy_analysis: The founding problem is live and the arrangement's core function has not atrophied, so no whole-constraint mandatrophy is declared. However, the consent-and-transparency SUBSYSTEM shows classic Goodhart drift: theater_ratio crosses 0.4 by interval end as proxy compliance (formal consent, boilerplate assessment) substitutes for the protective function the mechanism was built for. The temporal series exists precisely to let the engine distinguish subsystem decay from whole-constraint decay: if theater continues rising while enforcement stagnates, the consent subsystem approaches inertial maintenance even while the broader regime remains a functioning hybrid — a candidate for decomposition into a separate story if the divergence widens.
commentary.kernel_context: This story instantiates the autonomy_rights_reading of the kernel human_dignity_ai_safeguarding: dignity grounded in human autonomy, rationality, and rights rather than in divine image. The sibling readings — imago_dei_reading (dignity as the inviolable image of the Triune God, equal in all persons prior to any capability) and posthumanist_reading (the human is not a fixed limit; dignity attaches to persons however constituted) — are separate constraints with their own epsilon, victim sets, and enhancement permissiveness, linked through network.affects_constraints. The epsilon authored here measures the standing autonomy-rights safeguarding arrangement as this reading itself assesses it — never the arrangements the siblings would build. Reading relations: this reading FORECLOSES the imago_dei_reading because the two premises are contradictories on the same question (this reading's 'rather than divine image' negates the sibling's exclusive divine-image ground; no single framework can hold both as ultimate grounds), and INFLUENCES the posthumanist_reading because the autonomy settlement's institutional dominance channels enhancement and synthetic-person claims into rights-compliant forms without rendering posthumanism incoherent — transhumanist liberalism holds both.

omegas.question: This constraint is one reading — autonomy_rights_reading — of the kernel human_dignity_ai_safeguarding; the sibling readings imago_dei_reading and posthumanist_reading instantiate different constraints. Which reading governs a given jurisdiction's safeguarding regime, and how does the family classify as a set?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Generate and classify each sibling as its own story; compare victim sets, enhancement permissiveness, and epsilon across the family; track which ground dominates regulatory preambles and court reasoning over time.
omegas.impact: If the imago_dei_reading governed, enhancement limits tighten and theological grounds become admissible evidence, changing the suppression profile entirely; if the posthumanist_reading governed, the victim set expands to enhanced and synthetic persons and the autonomy premise itself becomes contestable. Classification of this file covers only the autonomy-rights arrangement.
omegas.description: Committer structure: this story is one of three readings of a contested dignity kernel; siblings are separate constraints, not hedges inside this one.

omegas.question: Where exactly do the three readings disagree — and the answer is at the ground of dignity (divine image vs. rational autonomy vs. constitution-independent personhood), not at the policy surface. How does the ground-level dispute propagate into structurally different constraints?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Trace the propagation: the ground determines admissible evidence (theological vs. psychological vs. metaphysical), the bearer class (humans vs. persons however constituted), and enhancement policy — verify that each sibling story's victim set and epsilon diverge for exactly these reasons.
omegas.impact: Identical regulations receive different justifications, different failure modes, and different extraction profiles under each ground; mislocating the dispute at the policy level would wrongly merge the family into one constraint.
omegas.description: The kernel contest is located at the foundation of dignity, which is why the readings cannot be averaged.

omegas.question: Is the theatrical component of consent and transparency mechanisms separable from their protective function?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Compare jurisdictions where penalties bite hardest: if enforcement intensity reduces consent formalism without losing protection, the components are separable and redesign (collective consent, fiduciary duties) can strip the theater.
omegas.impact: If inseparable, part of the measured theater is the irreducible price of mass-scale consent and the theater ratio overstates decay; if separable, the formalism is removable overhead and the subsystem's trajectory is worse than it looks.
omegas.description: Whether consent formalism is contingent design or structural to any workable mass-consent regime.

omegas.question: Do compliance costs actually confer durable relative advantage on incumbents, or are they absorbed competitively or passed through to users?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Entry-rate and firm-size-distribution analysis in heavily regulated versus lightly regulated AI segments; incidence studies of who ultimately bears conformity spending.
omegas.impact: Confirms or overturns incumbent_ai_platforms as the seat where the arrangement's gains accrue; if gains diffuse, the receipt surface is misdescribed and the extraction picture flattens toward diffuse.
omegas.description: Whether the compliance asymmetry is a real moat or a transient cost.

omegas.question: Is the marginalization of non-rights dignity vocabularies structural (admissibility rules of the consultative process) or internalized (advocates preemptively translate or self-censor before submission)?
omegas.resolution_mechanism: Discourse analysis of consultation records: count submissions in non-rights vocabularies and their fate versus rights-framed equivalents; interview excluded advocates about whether they were barred or pre-conformed.
omegas.impact: If internalized, opening procedural channels would not restore the excluded voices — the suppression would persist after the barrier is removed, meaning effective suppression exceeds the structural measure and carries beyond any procedural reform.
omegas.description: Structural versus internalized mechanism behind the exclusion of rival dignity registers.

network.dual_formulation_note: 'Human dignity in AI safeguarding' is a colloquial label covering three structurally distinct constraints distinguished by the ground of dignity (epsilon-invariance decomposition). This story authors the autonomy-rights member: epsilon ~0.46 measured on the standing autonomy-rights arrangement as that reading assesses it. The imago_dei_reading authors the same regulatory surface from a capability-independent divine-image ground — higher epsilon where enhancement-permissive provisions are concerned, and a victim set extending to embryo-, end-of-life-, and enhancement-adjacent interests this reading does not count. The posthumanist_reading authors it with the bearer class opened to enhanced and synthetic persons, making the exclusion of non-standard persons the central extraction. Upstream/downstream: the autonomy-rights settlement is institutionally dominant and therefore shapes both siblings' operating environment — it is cited as the reason theological grounds are inadmissible and serves as the template posthumanist claims must fit — without settling the ground dispute. All three files link one another through network.affects_constraints.
